perf: vectorize _get_tickers_series, split_ticker, ticker_df_to_qdf; guard reduce_df dedup [A/2 split of #2702]
body:
## What

Part **A** of splitting #2702 (`perf/qdf-panel-hotpaths`) into two independent PRs. This PR
is the clear net win — the categorical ticker/reduce vectorizations. It **excludes** the
`update_df` / `update_tickers` / `_concat_sort_dedup_qdf` rewrite, which is a net regression
on categorical fold-heavy pipelines and is held for rework (part B — see below).

## Why split

Benchmarking the economic-surprises pipeline (categorical `QuantamentalDataFrame` carried
end-to-end, folding a delta back with `update_df` ~20 times into a 13→37 M-row frame) showed
#2702's two halves pull in opposite directions, so they must not ship together:

1. **Ticker/reduce vectorizations** (`_get_tickers_series`, `split_ticker`, `ticker_df_to_qdf`
   / `qdf_to_ticker_df`, `reduce_df` dedup guard) — a clear win. **← this PR.**
2. **`update_df` rewrite** around a new `_concat_sort_dedup_qdf` (factorize + lexsort +
   single-pass dedup) — held; it materialises extra full-frame copies per call and, on the
   many-small-folds-into-a-growing-frame pattern, runs slower and hotter.

## Scope

- `types/qdf/methods.py`: `_get_tickers_series` (build tickers from codes on unique cid/xcat
  pairs), `reduce_df` (skip the terminal full-column `drop_duplicates` when the natural
  `(cid, xcat, real_date)` key is already unique).
- `utils/core.py`: `split_ticker` (factorize on unique tickers).
- `utils/df_utils.py`: `ticker_df_to_qdf` / `qdf_to_ticker_df` vectorization + import/cosmetic
  cleanup.
- **Excludes** every `update_df` / `update_tickers` / `_concat_sort_dedup*` hunk.

## Measured effect

Interleaved microbench on the real ~10.6M-row categorical panel (12 reps × 3 rounds; medians),
develop vs this branch — all three rounds agree:

| op | develop | this PR | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_get_tickers_series` | ~3,470–3,630 ms | **~410–470 ms** | **~7.7× faster** |
| `reduce_df` | ~550–590 ms | ~378–420 ms | **~25–31% faster** |
| `update_df` | ~4,500–5,070 ms | ~4,370–4,750 ms | **unchanged** (rewrite not included) |

In a full end-to-end build A/B, the `_get_tickers_series` speedup alone cut the `Basket`-heavy
`glb_baskets` cell by **~85 s** (156 → ~72 s) and `arma_norm` (ISC ticker derivation) by
~27 s. `Basket` is the pipeline's #1 remaining bottleneck, so this win lands directly.

## Correctness

Pure vectorization — output byte-identical to develop; no ordering/dedup semantics change (the
#2699 parity hashes still match). `update_df` behaviour and memory are untouched by this PR.

## Follow-ups

- **Part B** (`update_df` / `_concat_sort_dedup_qdf` rewrite) stays on `perf/qdf-panel-hotpaths`
  and needs rework before it can merge: it must show ≤ base wall **and** ≤ base peak RSS on the
  fold-heavy pipeline (avoid the double copy, batch folds caller-side, or a polars-backed
  concat+sort+dedup). Superseding this A-only PR, #2702 is being closed.

title: Feature: frequency-aware annualization (eop-cadence inference)
body:
## Summary

Adds **frequency-aware annualization** to `macrosynergy`, replacing a static, ticker-name-derived sqrt(1/freq) weighting that cannot represent an intra-series release-frequency change (e.g. **Australia CPI going quarterly -> monthly** in the same quantamental series).

Two pieces:

1. **`macrosynergy.management.utils.infer_release_frequency(eop, window=3, freqs=("D","W","M","Q","A"))`** - a pure, reusable classifier. It takes a per-observation `eop` (end-of-period) date series, computes the rolling-median gap between consecutive *distinct* eop dates, and snaps it to the nearest standard frequency in log space against `365.25 / ANNUALIZATION_FACTORS[freq]`. Revisions (shared eop) inherit the period's frequency; output is aligned to the input index.

2. **`macrosynergy.panel.annualize_by_release_frequency(df, xcats, cids, eop_col="eop", window=3, freqs=..., postfix="A")`** - a QDF transform. Per `(cid, xcat)` group it multiplies each value by `sqrt(1 / ANNUALIZATION_FACTORS[freq])`, where `freq` is the *contemporaneous* release frequency from the helper - so the weight is **time-varying** and flips at a genuine Q->M break.

```python
from macrosynergy.panel import annualize_by_release_frequency
dfa = annualize_by_release_frequency(dfx, xcats=[xc + "N" for xc in surprises], cids=cids)
```

## Design

- **Rolling-median estimator** (window 3, `min_periods=1`) is robust to one-off irregular releases; a real cadence break locks in within ~1 release (bounded by a test).
- **Reuses `ANNUALIZATION_FACTORS`** - no hard-coded 4/12 or period lengths; generalises the old sqrt(1/4)/sqrt(1/12) to `sqrt(1/apy)` for any supported frequency.
- **Requires an `eop` column** (as emitted by `InformationStateChanges.to_qdf(metrics=["eop", ...])`); raises a clear `ValueError` if absent rather than reconstructing from `eop_lag` (avoids a fragile holiday/business-day convention).
- Value-only QDF in -> out, categorical dtype preserved; empty-selection returns a uniform empty QDF (same type + column order as the normal path).

## Tests

- `tests/unit/management/test_frequency.py` (5): pure monthly/quarterly, **Q->M structural break** (lag bounded), one-off jitter does not flip, revisions inherit, snap boundaries.
- `tests/unit/panel/test_annualize_by_release_frequency.py` (6): pure-monthly/quarterly weights match the old static factors, **break transition 0.5 -> sqrt(1/12)**, `ANNUALIZATION_FACTORS` reuse, missing-`eop` error, empty-selection contract.
- All 11 pass, output pristine.

## Notes

- Companion notebook wiring (keep `eop` through `to_qdf`, call the new transform) is a separate change in the `academy` repo.

title: Feature: add panel_ewm_sum (fast EWM moving sum on business-day grid)
body:
## Summary

Adds `panel_ewm_sum` â€” a fast, vectorised exponential moving **sum** of quantamental panels on a business-day grid â€” to `macrosynergy.panel`. It replaces the slow ~68-formula `panel_calculator` EWM loop used in the economic-surprises research pipeline (which does one pivot/melt/`eval`/`concat` *per category*) with a single pivot â†’ business-day reindex â†’ `.ewm(halflife).sum()` sweep â†’ stack.

```python
from macrosynergy.panel import panel_ewm_sum
dfa = panel_ewm_sum(dfx, xcats=armanas, cids=cids, halflife=5)   # -> *_5DXMS categories
```

## Design

- **Business-day grid, zero-fill.** Sparse inputs are reindexed to a dense business-day grid and interior gaps zero-filled, so `halflife` is measured in **business days** (not release events). This is the intended `NDXMS` ("N-day exponential moving sum") semantics; the region before each series' first observation is excluded from the output.
- **Value-only QDF in â†’ out**, categorical dtype preserved; `halflife` accepts a scalar or list (`[3, 5]` â†’ `_3DXMS`, `_5DXMS`); optional `postfix` override; `cids`/`xcats`/`start`/`end`/`blacklist` supported. `blacklist` excludes the blacklisted (cid, date) ranges from the output.
- Uses pandas `.ewm(halflife).sum()` semantics â€” distinct from `management.utils.math.ewm_sum` (`ewm().mean()Ã—cumulative-weights`), which is cross-referenced in the docstring.

## Behavioural lock

A test asserts that on an already-dense daily-`B` panel, `panel_ewm_sum` is **numerically identical** to `panel_calculator`'s EWM-sum on the shared region (verified: full 260-row exact match), with a companion test showing it deliberately diverges on sparse input (business-day vs per-event decay). This pins densification as the *only* intended behavioural difference from the old loop.

## Tests

`tests/unit/panel/test_panel_ewm_sum.py` â€” 13 tests: basic decay + naming, zero-fill/leading-region, multi-halflife + postfix, equivalence + sparse divergence, subsetting/blacklist (input exclusion + output masking)/categorical round-trip/degenerate + empty-selection. All pass; full `tests/unit/panel/` suite green (205 passed, no regressions).

title: Feature: optional robust covariance estimators for CategoryRelations.ols_table
body:
optional robust standard errors in `ols_table`

Adds an opt-in `cov_type` (and `cov_kwds`) to `CategoryRelations.ols_table`, passed through to the statsmodels pooled fit, with panel-aware defaults:

- `cov_type="cluster"` — clusters by cross-section (`cid`).
- `cov_type="hac-groupsum"` / `"nw-groupsum"` — Driscoll-Kraay, using the `real_date` periods with the standard automatic lag choice and normal-based inference (the group-summed HAC estimators have no small-sample t degrees-of-freedom correction, which otherwise yields NaN p-values).
- `cov_kwds` overrides any of these defaults.

`ols_table` now also returns the fitted results object (in addition to printing the summary), so the covariance choice can be inspected programmatically. The default path (`cov_type=None`, i.i.d. standard errors) and the printed output are unchanged. `cov_type` is only valid with `type="pool"`; combining it with `type="re"` raises `ValueError`.

Clustered and Driscoll-Kraay standard errors are the standard correction for cross-sectional and serial dependence in macro panels (Petersen 2009; Driscoll-Kraay via Hoechle 2007), so the classic i.i.d. errors this currently defaults to can be materially over-confident on persistent panels.

**Tests.** Adds tests that the returned results match a direct statsmodels fit, that the robust options change the standard errors but not the coefficients (and yield finite p-values), that the cluster default matches a direct clustered fit, and that `type="re"` + `cov_type` raises.

title: Bugfix: harden corr_prob_calc panel-test p-value and fix PosRatio map_pval
body:
Two hardening fixes in the MAP panel-test code path, on functions the recent map_pval refactor (6fe7a573) did not touch.

**1. `CategoryRelations.corr_prob_calc` — read the p-value from the results object, with guards.** `corr_prob_calc` still fits `sm.MixedLM` and extracts the slope p-value with `re.summary().tables[1].iloc[1, 3]` — a rendered string, rounded to three decimals and dependent on the table layout — with no error handling. On a singular/collinear panel the fit raises an uncaught `LinAlgError`, and a non-estimable coefficient makes `float("")` raise `ValueError`, both propagating out of `reg_scatter`. This reads `re.pvalues` directly (full precision, layout-independent) and guards the degenerate cases so they warn and return `NaN` — the same treatment `SignalReturnRelations.map_pval` already has. (Migrating `corr_prob_calc` to the `RandomEffects` estimator, as `map_pval` was just refactored to do, would be a natural follow-up; this PR keeps the change minimal.)

**2. `SignalReturnRelations` — `PosRatio` for `map_pval` was always `NaN`.** In `__output_table__` the PosRatio row for `map_pval` computed `np.mean(np.array(map_pval_bool) * np.nan)` — multiplying by `np.nan`, so the result was unconditionally `NaN`. It now mirrors the `pearson_pval`/`kendall_pval` rows: the share of segments (where the panel test is defined) with error probability < 0.5 and positive correlation, staying `NaN` for single-cross-section segments.

**Tests.** Adds a regression test for each. Rebased onto current `develop`; the earlier `map_pval` p-value/guard changes were dropped as they're already covered by the recent refactor.

title: Bugfix: Basket accepts categorical QuantamentalDataFrame input [3/4 split of #2695]
body:
## Summary

**Part 3 of 4** splitting #2695 (kept open for reference on `feature/performance`). A standalone, minimal bug fix.

## The bug

`Basket.make_weights` trimmed leading all-NA rows with `dfw_wgs[fvi:]`, where `fvi` is a `real_date` **label** (a `Timestamp`). On the wide weight frame built from a **categorical** `QuantamentalDataFrame`, that index no longer supports positional `__getitem__` slicing with a label, so pandas raises:

```
pandas.errors.InvalidIndexError: slice(Timestamp('2010-12-01 00:00:00'), None, None)
```

…and `Basket` cannot be constructed from categorical QDF input. Object-dtype QDFs happened to work only because `frame[ts:]` on a `DatetimeIndex` is already label-based.

## The fix

```diff
-        dfw_wgs = dfw_wgs[fvi:]
+        dfw_wgs = dfw_wgs.loc[fvi:]
```

Explicit label-based slicing. **Byte-identical** for the object-dtype path (same rows), and it makes the categorical path work.

## Test (proves the bug)

Adds `tests/unit/panel/test_basket_performance.py`. Verified:
- **On `develop` (old code):** `test_categorical_qdf_parity` **fails** with the `InvalidIndexError` above (1 failed, 11 passed).

title: Refactor: reuse RandomEffects (Swamy–Arora) for the MAP panel test in SignalReturnRelations.map_pval
body:
cc @Magnus167

## What
Pivots this PR from a hand-rolled estimator to **reuse**. `SignalReturnRelations.map_pval`
(the Macrosynergy Panel / MAP significance p-value) now delegates to the package's existing
period random-effects estimator `macrosynergy.learning.random_effects.RandomEffects`
(**Swamy–Arora feasible GLS**), fitted as `signal ~ 1 + return` with a fixed intercept and
random effects grouped by `real_date`. The ~145-line bespoke closed-form ML estimator from
the earlier revision of this PR is removed, along with the now-unused `import statsmodels.api as sm`.

## Why the change of approach
- **Single source of truth.** The MAP test now lives in one team-owned, already-tested
  estimator instead of a second parallel implementation. (Note: `panel/category_relations.py`
  still runs its own `MixedLM(reml=False)` — a candidate for the same consolidation later.)
- **More statistically defensible.** Swamy–Arora uses **dof-corrected** variance components
  (like REML). The previous path (statsmodels `MixedLM.fit(reml=False)`) is plain ML, which
  omits that correction and mildly **overstates** significance in finite samples — and here the
  number of dates (groups) is a large fraction of N, so the correction is not negligible.
- **Performance.** ~30× faster than the statsmodels MixedLM optimizer it replaces (removes the
  lbfgs→cg retry cascade on near-boundary panels), meeting the original perf goal.

## Behaviour / compatibility
- **Public API unchanged:** same `map_pval(self, ret_vals, sig_vals)` signature, `float`/`np.nan`
  return, 3dp rounding, same warning messages.
- **Not bit-identical — a different (more defensible) estimator, not a reproduction.**
  Swamy–Arora vs the previous ML: p-value agrees to **~3–5e-3** (worst ≈0.005 over 324 panels),
  with **zero significance-decision flips** at the 0.9 threshold (only 2 knife-edge flips in a
  1200-panel boundary-stacked sweep — inherent to comparing two estimators at a hard cutoff).
  The slope differs by ~5e-4 (moments- vs likelihood-based variance ratio).
- **Degenerate designs → `np.nan` + warning:** ≤1 cid, missing `cid` level, singular/collinear
  design, and — via a new guard — a **constant/near-constant-variance signal or return** (which
  under a naive swap could otherwise produce a spurious *significant* p-value).
- **statsmodels stays a dependency** (used by 8 other modules incl. `make_qdf`); only the SRR
  `sm` import is removed.

## Tests
`TestMapPvalEstimator` rewritten to validate the RandomEffects path against a statsmodels
`MixedLM(reml=False)` oracle (slope agreement, p-value tolerance, zero decision-flips over a
seed sweep), plus grouping-by-date invariance, determinism, 3dp rounding, unit-interval,
signature tripwire, and **new regression tests** for the degenerate paths (a constant signal
must return `nan`, not false significance). `tests/unit/signal` is green (37 in the file,
41 in the dir).

body:
In the current code, hedge_calculator computed the estimation window start by indexing into the re-estimation dates (rdates) by max_obs, treating max_obs as a number of re-estimation periods rather than daily observations as documented. With the default monthly frequency and max_obs=1000, this always clamped to the first re-estimation date, so every beta was calculated using an expanding window from inception and max_obs had no effect.
 
 This PR changes the logic so the window beta is estimated over is now built from the last max_obs daily observations up to each re-estimation date.

These changes impact certain cells in the following academy notebooks:
* Inventories and metal returns
* Economic surprises and commodity futures returns
* Introduction to Macrosynergy package

Feature: collapse constant index levels + xcat_labels / axis_label_levels on single_statistic_table heatmap
body:
## Summary

Three opt-in extensions to `SignalReturnRelations.single_statistic_table` for heatmap rendering. **Default behaviour is byte-identical to before this PR** — every change is gated behind a new kwarg or fires only when the caller leaves an existing kwarg at `None`. The returned DataFrame is unchanged in every case.

- **`collapse_constant_levels: bool = False`** — when True, row/column index levels whose values are constant across the table are stripped from the tick labels and auto-promoted into the corresponding axis label (joined by `" · "`) when the caller did not pass `xlabel`/`ylabel` (or `row_names`/`column_names`). A table that iterates over one signal, one aggregation, and several frequencies renders only the frequencies as y-ticks and places `"<signal> · <aggregation>"` on the y-axis label. Default `False` preserves the historical rendering (raw MultiIndex tuples as tick labels).
- **`xcat_labels: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None`** — single rename dictionary covering both signal and return xcats. Internally split by membership in `self.sigs` / `self.rets` and routed through the existing `signal_name_dict` / `return_name_dict` machinery; unlisted xcats are kept verbatim so callers can't accidentally drop entries. Mutually exclusive with the legacy two dicts (raises if both supplied). Renamed values flow through to the auto axis label when `collapse_constant_levels=True`.
- **`axis_label_levels: Optional[List[str]] = None`** — list of level keys (`"xcat"`, `"ret"`, `"freq"`, `"agg_sigs"`) eligible for promotion into the auto axis label. Requires `collapse_constant_levels=True` (raises `ValueError` otherwise). Default `None` promotes every collapsed level. Passing `axis_label_levels=["xcat"]` drops aggregation/frequency suffixes from the auto label without putting them back on the ticks.

### Before / after (opt-in case)

Same call, same data — caller opts in to the new kwargs:

**Before** — caller passes `ylabel="Factor (feature) · aggregation · frequency"` because the y-tick labels would otherwise be opaque MultiIndex tuples like `("PFMONC_ZN", "last", "M")`.

**After** — drop the `ylabel` override; pass `collapse_constant_levels=True, axis_label_levels=["xcat"]`. Y-ticks become `M` / `Q`; y-axis label becomes `PFMONC_ZN` (or whatever the user passes via `xcat_labels`).

### Default-behaviour invariant

A reviewer flagged that the original version of this PR changed default rendering when callers had constant-valued levels and no explicit `xlabel`/`ylabel`. The `collapse_constant_levels=False` gate now removes that footgun: callers who don't touch the new kwargs get the same `view_table` inputs they did before.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/signal/test_signal_return_relations.py` — all 20 tests pass (4 new, 1 updated). Includes an explicit assertion that the default path produces no auto y-label / no tick collapse, plus a `ValueError` assertion when `axis_label_levels` is passed without the gate.
- [x] Heatmaps re-rendered end-to-end via the Monetary Conditions Power Factor academy notebook; 20/20 code cells run cleanly with the new kwargs opted in.
- [x] Backward compatibility: callers who pass `xlabel`/`ylabel` explicitly continue to see those exact strings (auto-label only fires when the caller leaves the kwarg `None`); callers who omit all new kwargs see byte-identical rendering inputs to pre-PR.
- [ ] Reviewer sanity-check on docstring wording, the `xcat_labels` / legacy-dict mutual-exclusion behaviour, and the `axis_label_levels` requires-gate validation.

Feature: `DataQueryFileAPIClient` - functionality to read delta files
body:
Install using:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/macrosynergy/macrosynergy@feature/dq-delta-files
```

---

# DataQueryFileAPIClient - example calls

This guide shows representative usage patterns for reviewers to quickly understand intended API flows and edge cases.

---

## 1. Instantiate client + inspect availability

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

client = DataQueryFileAPIClient()

df = client.list_available_files_for_all_file_groups()
df.head()
```

Purpose:

* Validates auth
* Confirms API connectivity
* Surfaces file-group / vintage structure

---

## 2. Daily workflow: full snapshot download

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

client = DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data")
client.download_full_snapshot()
```

Notes:

* Recommended daily sync
* Uses local on-disk cache
* Includes full snapshots, deltas, metadata

---

## 3. `download()` — filtered pull (cid / xcat schema)

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

with DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data") as client:
    df = client.download(
        cids=["AUD", "CAD", "USD", "JPY"],
        xcats=["EQXR_NSA", "RIR_NSA"],
        start_date="2000-01-01",
    )
```

Notes:

* Main "one-stop" method
* Triggers snapshot/delta download if needed
* Returns pandas DataFrame by default

---

## 3b. `download()` — ticker schema

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

with DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data") as client:
    df = client.download(
        tickers=["USD_RIR_NSA", "EUR_RIR_NSA", "JPY_RIR_NSA"],
        metrics=["value"],
        start_date="2015-01-01",
        dataframe_format="tickers",
    )

    wide = df.pivot(index="real_date", columns="ticker", values="value")
```

Notes:

* Preserves `ticker` column
* Convenient for modeling / matrix ops

---

## 3c. Large requests — Polars (lazy)

```python
import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

with DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data") as client:
    catalog = pd.read_parquet(client.download_catalog_file())
    tickers = catalog[catalog["Ticker"].str.startswith(("USD_", "EUR_"))]["Ticker"]

    lf = client.download(
        tickers=tickers.tolist(),
        start_date="2010-01-01",
        metrics=["value", "last_updated"],
        dataframe_type="polars-lazy",
        include_file_column=True,
    )

    df = lf.filter(pl.col("real_date") >= pl.date(2020, 1, 1)).collect()
```

Notes:

* Avoids materializing large frames prematurely
* Intended for power users / batch jobs

---

## 4. Incremental updates (delta + metadata only)

```python
import pandas as pd
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

client = DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data")

since = (pd.Timestamp.utcnow() - pd.DateOffset(days=10)).strftime("%Y%m%d")

client.download_full_snapshot(
    since_datetime=since,
    include_full_snapshots=False,
    include_delta=True,
    include_metadata=True,
)
```

Notes:

* Skips full snapshots
* Useful for catch-up jobs

---

## 5. Download a specific historical file

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

client = DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data")

path = client.download_file(
    filename="JPMAQS_MACROECONOMIC_BALANCE_SHEETS_20250414.parquet"
)
```

Notes:

* Filename discovered via availability listings
* Bypasses snapshot logic

---

## 6. Inspect a single file-group

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

client = DataQueryFileAPIClient()

df = client.list_available_files(
    file_group_id="JPMAQS_MACROECONOMIC_BALANCE_SHEETS"
)

df.iloc[-1]  # earliest available vintage
```

---

## 7. Metadata notifications (missing data & revisions)

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient

with DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./jpmaqs_data") as client:
    missing = client.get_missing_data_notifications(date="2026-01-19")
    revisions = client.get_revisions_notifications(date="2026-01-19")
```

Purpose:

* Surface missing updates
* Track historical revisions


## 8. Download a slice of the dataset "as of" a specific date-time.

This method downloads the necessary snapshot and delta files to reconstruct the dataset as of the specified date-time.

```python
from macrosynergy.download import DataQueryFileAPIClient
import pandas as pd

tickers = ['AUD_EQXR_NSA', 'CAD_EQXR_NSA', 'USD_EQXR_NSA', 'JPY_EQXR_NSA']

with DataQueryFileAPIClient(out_dir="./data/jpmaqs-data/") as dq:
    # Cut off at noon on 2025-11-12 (UTC)
    df = dq.download_as_of(tickers=tickers, as_of_datetime="2025-11-12T12:00:00")

    # inline with T-1 release schedule
    assert df['real_date'].max() <= pd.Timestamp("2025-11-12")
    assert df['last_updated'].max() <= pd.Timestamp("2025-11-12T12:00:00")
    print(df.head())
```

Add the option to score information state changes by either `diff` (default) or `level`.

In a previous PR (https://github.com/macrosynergy/macrosynergy/pull/2235), we modified for the normalisation, but not how we filtered to new information. Hence new information was captured as: `abs(Y(t) - Y(t-1)) > 0`

title: Feature: Categorical DataFrame
body:
Example code:
```python
from macrosynergy.management.types import QuantamentalDataFrame
from macrosynergy.management.simulate import make_test_df
from macrosynergy.management.utils import reduce_df
from typing import List
import pandas as pd

cids = ["USD", "EUR", "JPY", "GBP", "AUD", "CAD", "CHF", "SEK"]
xcats = ["FX", "IR", "EQ", "CR", "CO", "FI", "IN", "CM", "ME", "OT"]


df: pd.DataFrame = make_test_df(cids=cids, xcats=xcats)

dfc = df.copy()
print(f"Size of pd.DataFrame: {df.memory_usage(deep=True).sum() / 1024 ** 2} MB")

df = QuantamentalDataFrame(df)  # memory free!

qdf = QuantamentalDataFrame(dfc)  # new copy created, no memory freed

print(f"Size of QDF: {qdf.memory_usage(deep=True).sum() / 1024 ** 2} MB")
print("Is Categorical:", qdf.is_categorical())

red_df = qdf.reduce_df(cids=["USD", "EUR"], xcats=["FX", "IR"])

red_df.reduce_df(cids=["USD"], xcats=["FX"], inplace=True)

wdf: pd.DataFrame = qdf.to_wide()

try:
    test_if_qdf = QuantamentalDataFrame(wdf)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")
    print("-- Expected : DataFrame is not a QuantamentalDataFrame --")


test_df = QuantamentalDataFrame(df)


def example_func(test_df: QuantamentalDataFrame, cids: List[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if not isinstance(test_df, QuantamentalDataFrame):
        raise TypeError("Expected: QuantamentalDataFrame")
    
    if type(test_df) is QuantamentalDataFrame:
        return test_df.reduce_df(cids=cids)
    else:
        return reduce_df(df=test_df, cids=cids)

```

NumPy 1.22.0 is a big release featuring the work of 153 contributors spread over 609 pull requests. There have been many improvements, highlights are:

Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 1.21.6 to 1.22.0.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v1.22.0

NumPy 1.22.0 Release Notes

NumPy 1.22.0 is a big release featuring the work of 153 contributors spread over 609 pull requests. There have been many improvements, highlights are:

  • Annotations of the main namespace are essentially complete. Upstream is a moving target, so there will likely be further improvements, but the major work is done. This is probably the most user visible enhancement in this release.
  • A preliminary version of the proposed Array-API is provided. This is a step in creating a standard collection of functions that can be used across application such as CuPy and JAX.
  • NumPy now has a DLPack backend. DLPack provides a common interchange format for array (tensor) data.
  • New methods for quantile, percentile, and related functions. The new methods provide a complete set of the methods commonly found in the literature.
  • A new configurable allocator for use by downstream projects.

These are in addition to the ongoing work to provide SIMD support for commonly used functions, improvements to F2PY, and better documentation.

The Python versions supported in this release are 3.8-3.10, Python 3.7 has been dropped. Note that 32 bit wheels are only provided for Python 3.8 and 3.9 on Windows, all other wheels are 64 bits on account of Ubuntu, Fedora, and other Linux distributions dropping 32 bit support. All 64 bit wheels are also linked with 64 bit integer OpenBLAS, which should fix the occasional problems encountered by folks using truly huge arrays.

Expired deprecations

Deprecated numeric style dtype strings have been removed

Using the strings "Bytes0", "Datetime64", "Str0", "Uint32", and "Uint64" as a dtype will now raise a TypeError.

(gh-19539)

Expired deprecations for loads, ndfromtxt, and mafromtxt in npyio

numpy.loads was deprecated in v1.15, with the recommendation that users use pickle.loads instead. ndfromtxt and mafromtxt were both deprecated in v1.17 - users should use numpy.genfromtxt instead with the appropriate value for the usemask parameter.

title: Feature: `ProxyPnL` calculations including transaction costs
body:
Docs URL: https://docs.macrosynergy.com/feature-proxy_pnl/macrosynergy.pnl.html

---
Setting out the draft PR for proxy PnL as a means of having an easy review place for @sandresen1 and @emhbrine to review and catch up with the work @Magnus167 and I have done. Before we merge it in (once every functionality is completed), we should make sure to sit down the four of us and review together.

Outstanding features:
- [x] Implement relative value in contract signals.
- [x] Complete first implementation of volatility targeted notional positions. 
- [x] Rebalance frequency of notional positions need to respect rebalance dates (and stay constant between dates).
- [x] Historic portfolio volatility: make look-back periods and half-life parameters per estimation frequency (check vol-target from JPMaQS).
- [x] Change rebalance frequency in notional positions to be first business day of the month (instead of end of month).
- [x] Calculate PnL without transaction costs for notional positions: `PNL = FX_POS * FXXR_NSA` (plus accumulation of position value).
- [x] Build inter- and extrapolation class for transaction costs (bid-offers and spread).
- [x] Calculate Transaction costs: `TC = |Delta FX_POS| * Spread(|FX_POS|)` (trading costs) , and `RC = |Avg(FX_POS, rebalance freq)| * RollCosts(|FX_POS|)` (roll costs).
- [x] Calculate PnL ex. transaction costs: `PNL_EX_COSTS = PNL - TC - RC`.

Misc features:
- [x] Ability to extract (and to plot) the expected portfolio volatility (as well as estimate the realised portfolio volatility.
- [x] Class method to plot the time-series of the correlations and volatility from the variance covariance matrices at the rebalance dates.
- [x] Ability to plot transaction costs curves (functions) for both bid-offer spread and roll costs.

Feature: Adding `granger_causality_test()`
body:
Added a function that runs a Granger causality test with the following parameters and dosctrings.
```
Run Granger Causality Test on a standardized quantamental dataframe.
Since the Graner Causality Test is a pairwise test, only two tickers can be specified.
Specify either `tickers` or `cids` & `xcats`. When specifying `cids` & `xcats`, the
user may input one `cid` and two `xcats`; or two `cids` and one `xcat` to yield two
tickers. The function forms the list of tickers from the `cids` and `xcats` such that
the order of the formed tickers is preserved. The order of the tickers is important
as the first ticker is the one that is tested to Granger cause the second ticker.
The function tests whether the first ticker Granger causes the second ticker.

:param <pd.DataFrame> df: A standardized quantamental dataframe.
:param <List[str]> tickers: A list of tickers to run the test on. A maximum of two
    tickers can be specified.
:param <Union[str, List[str]]> cids: One or two cids to run the test on. If two cids
    are specified, then only one xcat can be specified. If one cid is specified, then
    two xcats can be specified.
:param <Union[str, List[str]]> xcats: One or two xcats to run the test on. If two
    xcats are specified, then only one cid can be specified. If one xcat is specified,
    then two cids can be specified.
:param <Union[int, List[int]]> max_lag: If `max_lag` is an integer, then the function
    computes the test for all lags up to `max_lag`. If `max_lag` is a list of integers,
    then the function computes the test only for lags specified in the list.
:param <bool> add_constant: Whether to add a constant to the regression.
:param <str> freq: The frequency to downsample the data to. Must be one of "D", "W",
    "M", "Q", "A". Default is "M".
:param <str> agg: The aggregation method to use when downsampling the data. Must be
    one of "mean" (default), "median", "min", "max", "first" or "last".
:param <str> start: The start date of the data. Must be a valid ISO date. If not
    specified, the earliest date in `df` is used.
:param <str> end: The end date of the data. Must be a valid ISO date. If not
    specified, the latest date in `df` is used.
:param <str> metric: The metric to run the test on. Must be a column in `df`.
    Default is "value".
```

title: Feature : Refactor `view_timelines`
body:
[macrosynergy.panel.view_timelines()](https://github.com/macrosynergy/macrosynergy/blob/develop/macrosynergy/panel/view_timelines.py) has had issues to do with alignment and passing the correct directives to the backends - matplotlib and seaborn.
Since matplotlib operates on mostly global runtime settings, seaborn is able to overwrite and use these; however for our purposes the crossover causes a lot of headaches where directives to the backends interfere and cause undesirable behaviour.

The new refactor uses only matplotlib with the special addition of `plt.tight_layout()` - which uses a form of constraint solver to achieve a desired state. This now allows us to use `view_timelines()` with very minimal adjustment/additional arguments, except for data args and most likely size.

Even though one may not need any adjustments

Changed defaults:
`all_xticks: bool = True` ~`False`~


New arguments added :
```python
"""
:param <int> label_fontsize: font size of labels. Default is 12.

:param <str> legend_loc: location of legend. Default is 'lower center'.
    The options are (strings) 'upper left', 'upper right', 'lower left',
    'lower right', 'upper center', 'lower center', 'center left', 'center right'.
    The string 'best' places the legend at the location, among the nine locations
    defined so far, with the minimum overlap with other drawn features.
    One can also pass a tuple (x, y) in axes coordinates to specify the
    bottom-left corner of the legend. The coordinates (0, 0) are the
    bottom-left corner of the plot's area (chart+labels).
    Please see matplotlib documentation for more details -
    https://matplotlib.org/stable/api/_as_gen/matplotlib.pyplot.legend.htm
"""
```
-----------------------

Setting the new `legend_loc='best'` when using single charts now allows for the legend to be dynamically moved without user-input based on the least "busy" or simply the "best" location for the legend.

title: Bugfix in business_day_dif
body: Python Datetime's/Pandas' `isocalender()` represents a date in the form (Year, Week number, Week day). One of the calculations was using an a deprecated form of getting the year for the calculations. Updating the code to use `pd.DatetimeIndex.isocalender()` fixed the issue. title: changed  "ci" keyword to "estimator" in sns.lineplot calls in view_timelines.py
body:
The "ci" (confidence interval) argument/keyword specifies a method for creating error-bars in lineplots  `seaborn` (up to and incl. version 11.2).
In `seaborn` version 12 onwards, this has been deprecated, and replaced by the `estimator` keyword, which allows the user to specify which estimator to use. 
The implication is that seaborn ignores the argument, and goes on to run error-bar estimation calculations on the data.
It is does not cause a single lineplot to be significantly slower, however when using a panel with multiple lineplots (seaborn.FacetGrid), the output takes much longer.

The issue is documented on the seaborn repository issues here : https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn/issues/3006
To which the solution (implemented in this commit) is also provided by repo. owner : https://github.com/mwaskom/seaborn/issues/3006#issuecomment-1241318307. 

The solution is backward compatible and needs to be implemented in other functions of the macrosynergy package that may use "ci" arguments for lineplots. It is compatible down to (and incl.) seaborn version 0.9.0 (July 2018).

title: Fixed bug arising due to a type error
body:
The error was due to NaN types in pandas dataframes. 
The code requires the dataframe values to be converted to numerical types. However, NaN cannot be represented in integers, as numpy (a core pandas dependency) does not provide this functionality. Therefore, we cast the values to floating-point numbers (floats) which provide functionality for NaN (as well as inf.).
This is a documented [pandas "gotcha"](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/gotchas.html).

Refs: 
https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/gotchas.html#support-for-integer-na
and
https://stackoverflow.com/a/21290084/4417821
